title: I Followed the Herbarium Press Hours Into the Folder They Took

parts.text: I opened press one at 11:06 a.m. and intern Willa was already lifting my numbered blotters. The card said: ONE PRESS. TEN DAYS. FOLDER STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-three, botany volunteer, holding a voucher that listed our sheet. Willa shrugged. "Interns are the press." I photographed the card, the booking, and her folder on my straps. Then I asked for the press log. At 11:14 collections pinged why Willa's name was on my blotters. I kept my voice herbarium-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Collections can see Willa's folder on my straps during our booking.

social.video_title: She lifted my numbered blotters from the press — Part 1/2
social.description: Herbarium press, an intern on my straps, a ten-day clock she posted. I logged the folder. Would you have asked for the press log?

parts.text: Willa called it a check until collections asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the folder still. The blotters went back to my straps. Willa ran her own ten days and told the next intern atmosphere was always about dry. Dry is a word interns use when a booking exists. Press policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE PRESS. I keep our voucher on a labeled clip. Willa brown-bags her jokes. The press finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns are not the press — Part 2/2
social.description: Press log, numbered blotters, and a second line on the card. Was a check ever my straps?
